data.title:
Find the Opening, Write the Post,
Measure What It Did
paragraphs: Writing on its own stopped being enough. We go into your Search Console and find the questions you already show up for and hardly ever get clicked on, write the post that answers one of them, put it in front of the people it was written for, and then show you in your own analytics what moved.
Your free growth audit reads your own data and tells you:

• The questions you already rank for on page two, which are the cheapest wins you have
  • Whether Google's AI names you when a buyer asks about your category, and who it names instead
  • The pages earning impressions and almost no clicks
  • What to write first, and the reason it is that one

items.title: Opportunity From Your Own Data
items.text: We start in your Search Console instead of a brainstorm. The queries where you already earn impressions and almost no clicks are the cheapest wins you have, and they are sitting in an account you already own and probably have not opened in a while.

items.title: A Dedicated Writer
items.text: You get one writer, and you keep them. They learn your voice, your industry and the things your customers ask, and they carry what they learned on the last post into the next one.

items.title: Written In Your Voice
items.text: We build a voice profile from your existing material and write against it, so a new post reads like the ones your team wrote before we showed up.

items.title: Targeted Social After It Publishes
items.text: A post nobody sees earns nothing while it waits for search to catch up, so each piece goes out with social written for the people it was aimed at, on the platforms where those people spend their time.

items.title: Measured In Your GA4
items.text: You see which posts brought people in, what they searched to get there, and what they did once they landed. Numbers out of your analytics, not a screenshot of ours.

items.title: Editorial Review
items.text: Each article gets fact-checked, edited and put through an SEO pass before it reaches you, so what lands in your inbox is ready to publish.

data.title: This Ain't Your Traditional Blog Service
data.subtitle: Four things have to happen before content earns anything, and most agencies sell you one of them. Which one are you paying for right now? We run all four, and the last one is how you find out whether the first three worked.

steps.title: We Read Your Search Console
steps.text: We pull your real query data and find where demand and outcome disagree, the pages earning impressions without clicks and the questions you rank for on page two.

steps.title: We Write the Post
steps.text: Your dedicated writer takes one of those openings and writes the piece that answers it, in your voice, reviewed by an editor before it reaches you.

steps.title: We Put It In Front of People
steps.text: Search takes months to reward a post, so targeted social carries it to the audience it was written for while the ranking builds, and the piece earns attention in week one rather than in month three.

steps.title: We Measure It In GA4
steps.text: Traffic, queries, and what visitors did after landing. That result picks the next topic, which is what makes this a loop instead of a content calendar.

paragraphs: A blog stops working the moment it becomes something you owe. The posts get shorter, the gaps get longer, and the archive turns into a record of the months you had time rather than a case for why anyone would buy from you.

Handing the blog to one writer who stays on your account changes what the archive becomes. That writer carries the context from the last post into the next one, so the library builds an argument over a year rather than restating an introduction twelve times.
If you want the longer version before you talk to anyone, we have written up what this work costs, how a blog writing service runs end to end, and what changes when the store is on Shopify.

items.question: How do you decide what to write about?
items.answer: We read your Search Console first. The best starting point is usually a question you already rank for on page two, because Google has told you there is demand and told you that you are close. You approve the topics before anyone writes anything.

items.question: What does the social part involve?
items.answer: Each article goes out with social written for the audience that article was aimed at, on the platforms where that audience spends time. Search takes months to reward a post, and social gets it read while you wait.

items.question: How do I know it worked?
items.answer: We report out of your GA4 and your Search Console, so the numbers are yours and you can check them without us. You see which posts brought traffic, which queries they landed for, and what people did after they arrived.

items.question: How many blog posts do I get per month?
items.answer: Most plans run 4 to 8 articles a month, and we go to 16 and beyond for teams pushing harder. Starting at 4 and raising it once you can see what is working is usually the sensible way in.

items.question: How much does this cost?
items.answer: The work runs on a monthly plan set by how many articles you want and how long they run. One conversation is enough to scope it, and you get the number before you commit to anything.

items.question: Do I get the same writer every time?
items.answer: Yes. You are assigned a writer who learns your brand voice and your industry, and they stay on your account. That consistency is most of what makes an archive read like one company wrote it.

items.question: How long are the posts?
items.answer: Most run 800 to 1,500 words, though we write to the length the topic needs rather than to a number.

items.question: Can I request revisions?
items.answer: Yes, and they are included until you are happy with it. We would rather get it right than put something out that does not sound like you.
